A Ukrainian FP-5 Flamingo cruise missile flying at extremely low altitude during one of the missile strikes on Russia.
The exact date, location, and other details remain unknown.
The footage illustrates how low these missiles can fly, making them much harder to detect and intercept using conventional ground-based radar and air defense systems. This is where airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) aircraft play a critical role.
Russia could face growing challenges if Ukraine significantly expands production of these cruise missiles or acquires long-range cruise missiles from Western countries. The Russian Aerospace Forces (VKS) operate a limited number of AEW&C aircraft, making it difficult to maintain continuous radar coverage over such a vast territory and respond effectively to repeated large-scale cruise missile attacks.
